title: Upstream DHT and downstream AR/mechanical branches are actuator-distinct

known_answer.upstream_DHT_reduction: moves both A_AR and M in the synthetic branch model
known_answer.AR_specific_blockade: moves A_AR but leaves M unchanged
known_answer.mechanical_relaxation: moves M but leaves A_AR unchanged
known_answer.equal_reduced_burden_counterexample: AR-blocked and mechanics-relaxed states can both have reduced burden 0.5 while retaining opposite active branches

source_bound_motivation: Li et al. 2026 reports DHT-induced CTS hypercontraction through a GPR133-associated path; GPR133 knockdown or ML-7 reversed contractile/pathological effects, while AR knockdown alleviated HF growth inhibition without altering CTS contraction.
invariants: Upstream Ligand State != Receptor-Specific Signaling State
Equal Reduced Androgen Burden != Equal Residual Mechanism
Actuator Specificity Determines Required State Resolution
HF01_consequence: Future biological interpretation should not use one A scalar as if it simultaneously represented DHT exposure, AR signaling and every DHT-dependent noncanonical path. The original A may remain a reduced synthetic coordinate only when actuator distinctions are irrelevant to the question.
clinical_boundary: This is not a medication comparison or recommendation. In particular, an upstream DHT-lowering intervention and an AR antagonist are mechanistically different controls; the source experiment does not establish clinical superiority or treatment choice.
